S04.meta: // SLIDE 04 — THERAPEUTIC WINDOW: Too little → resistance; too much → lethal toxicity

modes.label: Sub-therapeutic
modes.resolves: Resistance emerges from surviving cells — tumor progresses

modes.label: Therapeutic window
modes.sub: Exploits tumor vulnerability over normal-tissue tolerance
modes.resolves: Tumor kill without life-threatening normal-tissue injury

modes.label: Supra-therapeutic
modes.resolves: Toxicities become life-threatening faster than tumor kill extends life

verdicts: window is narrow — normal tissue carries the same machinery the drug attacks
every dosing decision is an attempt to exploit or widen this gap

S07.meta: // SLIDE 07 — COMBINATION PRINCIPLES: Three rules that prevent single-mutation resistance

data.question: Why does combination chemotherapy beat single agents at cure?

branches.label: Single-agent therapy
branches.detail: One mechanism — one resistance mutation defeats the entire treatment. High proliferation + genomic instability make such mutations abundant.
branches.fix: Resistance arises readily — no curative potential for most cancers

branches.label: Combination — three rules
branches.detail: Different mechanisms + non-overlapping toxicities + each with single-agent activity. A single mutation cannot defeat all three simultaneously.
branches.fix: First curative regimens for Hodgkin, testicular cancer — uniformly fatal diseases

resolver.label: Combination as proof of concept
resolver.detail: MOPP cured Hodgkin. BEP cures most metastatic testicular cancer. The three rules are why.

S10.meta: // SLIDE 10 — TOXICITY TRACKING: Per-cycle (recoverable) vs cumulative (lifetime limit) toxicities

tracks.label: Per-cycle toxicities
tracks.outcome: Myelosuppression, nausea — dip after each dose, recover toward baseline. Managed with growth factors and dose timing.

tracks.label: Cumulative / lifetime-limit toxicities
tracks.outcome: Doxorubicin cardiomyopathy, bleomycin fibrosis, etoposide secondary AML — never reset. Tracked across all prior treatment.
